quest.title: Top Note: Floral Debt
quest.description: Port Ormos has been exceptionally lively lately. It looks like preparations for something big are underway...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Pomum de Ambra Chapter: Act I
chapter.title: Floral Debt, Blood Due

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...I thought I told him to spray it with water to retain moisture before applying the film?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You can't treat a Glaze Lily like a cactus... If Sanjay does this again, the loss will have to come out of his food expenses.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I'll go talk to him. At this rate, he won't even be able to afford eating cacti for much longer...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Tighnari!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh? It's you two! It's been a while! What brings you to Port Ormos?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We didn't have anything to do, and this place looked pretty lively, so we decided to stop by! But, uh... what's with all the flowers around here?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, Port Ormos is currently organizing a "Flower Exhibition" featuring flowers and plants from all over Teyvat, so I came to help out.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The exhibition includes flowers from every corner of the world, each with their own unique properties and needs. With that in mind, the curator commissioned a flower pot from Kshahrewar, capable of retaining heat and moisture...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Even so, an expert is still required to develop tailored transportation and care plans for each type of flower.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! And that expert is you, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Not this time, no. I'm just here to help out. The expert in charge is someone else...

dialogues.speaker: Neriman
dialogues.text: ...Mr. Tighnari! Sanjay, he... He confused the poisonous bulbs with garlic shoots, and he ate them!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Never mind, forget about what I said about the food expenses.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #Apologies, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. Looks like I've got something to take care of. I'll be back in just a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari's busy no matter where he is, huh...

choices.text: Too many people are careless about what they eat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, seems like it... Hey, don't look at Paimon like that! Paimon is super careful about what she eats!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, looks like Tighnari might be busy for a while. Let's take a look around the port in the meantime!

choices.text: Too many people don't do as they're told.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, seems like it! Some people just need supervision.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Look at these flowers! They smell so...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... ACHOO!
...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Achoo!

choices.text: Something wrong?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's... fine, she's just... got a little...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ..Aaah—Achoo! ACHOO!
...Rainbow Roses... Glaze Lilies... and Cecilias? No wonder...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It... It's getting worse... Why...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ACHOO!

choices.text: Maybe you're sick!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... Paimon was fine just a moment ago... She didn't even eat anything weird...
Ah, a moment of your time, you two... If it's not too much trouble, perhaps you could try this incense.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Incense? ...Oh, the scent is so nice... Wait!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You can talk normally now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woah... That was fast! Paimon doesn't have to sneeze anymore!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Must've been the incense! Thank you!
Think nothing of it! From your attire, I imagine you two aren't from Sumeru either...
Seeing as we're both travelers from abroad, it's only right that we help each other out should the occasion arise.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... So, you're here for the Flower Exhibition too?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Hm... I suppose that's accurate. Ah, allow me to introduce myself... I'm Emilie, a perfumer from Fontaine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon is Paimon! Thank you so much for your help just now! Oh, and this is...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, right? I've heard a lot about you from The Steambird. It's nice to finally put a face to the name.

choices.text: I've heard a lot about you as well...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What happened back there? Why did Paimon start sneezing all of a sudden...?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Hm... Have you ever heard of hay fever?

choices.text: I think so...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: To put it simply... When inhaled, certain pollens can trigger abnormal physical reactions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... But, Paimon has seen these kinds of flowers before, and nothing weird happened then...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Well, we're all different. The factors that can trigger a reaction to certain stimuli vary by person. In isolation, the effects of certain pollens may seem minimal, but inhaling various types at once can trigger a more overt reaction.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: But, there's no need to worry. Pollen allergies can be effectively mitigated with the use of medication.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, well, that's good...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #{NICKNAME}! Paimon! There you are... Is everything alright?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I left in such a hurry, I forgot to warn you about all the pollen in the air...

choices.text: Yeah, Paimon was not having a good time...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #Emilie? Ah, what a coincidence... Looks like my worry was misplaced, then. {NICKNAME} and Paimon are in good hands.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: It was nothing, really. We happened to run into each other shortly after my arrival, and I offered them a bit of help, that's all.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: #I'm more curious as to why you thought {NICKNAME} and Paimon were in danger... Allergies are highly unpredictable. If you were concerned the pollen might trigger a reaction, that must mean... something similar has happened in the past?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Something like that, yeah...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Remember the first time we met? You fainted after inhaling Spirit Borneol...

choices.text: That was an allergic reaction?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Spirit Borneol didn't affect Paimon at all, and now she's the one suffering... It makes no sense!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: It's not really something you can make sense out of, Paimon. There are all kinds of allergies out there, caused by a variety of different factors. Some people are even allergic to almonds... It's not something you can generalize.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Exactly. I even encountered a case in Fontaine where someone had an allergic reaction to Soba Noodles their family brought back from Inazuma...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woah... Good thing Paimon isn't allergic to anything delicious...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you a doctor, Emilie?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Hm... In a manner of speaking. Although, you could say the "patients" I deal with are rather unusual...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: In addition to medicine, Emilie is also very knowledgeable about botany. She's taught me a lot about the native flora around Fontaine.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: And that's where my expertise ends, I'm afraid. When it comes to breadth of knowledge, Tighnari certainly comes out on top.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A flower expert... Ah, Paimon's got it! You must be the expert Tighnari mentioned! The one in charge of the exhibition!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: ...Wrong again, I'm afraid.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Well, I did come for the exhibition, but only to inquire about the "Auguste" variety. I'm not involved in any official capacity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, Paimon was sure she got it right this time...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The "Auguste" variety? What's that?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: It's a kind of flower that was once popular in Fontaine. The perfume made from it also bears the same name... "Auguste."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Auguste," huh... That's not a name you hear often nowadays!

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: In an ancient language, the word is said to mean "sacred" or "noble." It's sometimes used as a name for people as well.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...Ah, that reminds me, are you familiar with the historical event in Fontaine known as the "Perfume Mania"?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Not really...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: The "Perfume Mania" was an event that occurred in Fontaine nearly twenty years ago...

choices.text: But, Paimon was the victim this time.
But, Emilie helped us out.
But, I don't know much about it.
Although, I didn't expect to run into you in Sumeru.
Should we go find Tighnari?
You feeling okay?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It all started when several merchants released their own lines of high-end, expensive perfumes, marketing them as must-have, luxury products, the very symbol of elegance itself...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: No one anticipated the absolute frenzy this would create on the market, causing the price of the perfumes to skyrocket.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: The demand was two-fold... What some saw as a status symbol, most saw as a money-making opportunity. You could take advantage of the soaring price by hoarding them and reselling at even higher margins.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: The value of these products became so inflated, regular bottles of perfume were even going for hundreds of thousands of Mora. This resulted in countless disputes and scams.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: But, at the end of the day, perfume is just perfume. The market value greatly exceeded the intrinsic worth of the product, creating an economic bubble that was never going to last.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Luckily, the Palais Mermonia recognized the danger and intervened before the craze could truly spread. Many profiteers and scammers were thrown in jail as a result.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: In the end, only a few wealthy families were affected when the bubble popped.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's good... It really could have been a lot worse.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What does all this have to do with that "Auguste" you mentioned earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Well, during the craze, the most popular perfume was none other than "Auguste." The demand far exceeded the supply, to the point where it once sold for ten million Mora a bottle.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: T—Ten million!? Then what about now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Calm down, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: After the mania ended, most perfumes returned to a normal price. "Auguste" was the only exception...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Its namesake, the flower used to create it, went extinct. As a result, no new bottles of "Auguste" have been made, and the value of the perfume remains exceedingly high.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The flower... went extinct?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Indeed. The Auguste flower was not a natural variety, you see. It was specially cultivated for use in perfume-making.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: When the bubble popped, all the flowerbeds used for its cultivation were destroyed in a fire. The variety has never been seen since...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... didn't you say you came to the exhibition to look for it?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. I came to investigate a certain rumor that the Auguste flower has reappeared in Sumeru... It's causing quite the stir in the Fontaine perfume market.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! We should help Emilie look for it!

choices.text: It's just a rumor, Paimon...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I have to agree. Emilie wrote me to ask if I could look into the rumor, but the Forest Rangers haven't received any reports of new plant species recently.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Even if I can locate the flower, I'm afraid you'll be disappointed, Paimon. I don't have any grand Mora-making endeavors planned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ehhhh!?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: "Divine," "noble," "one of a kind"... All beautiful sentiments, to be sure... But, to me, they overshadow the very essence of the product.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: When it comes to perfume, I want people to forget the price and the prestige... and focus on the beauty of the fragrance itself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow... So noble...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Of course, there's also a more practical reason... In recent years, low-grade, counterfeit versions of "Auguste" have been popping up on the Fontaine perfume market.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...Every so often, someone will claim to have recreated the unique scent of "Auguste," and the rumor mill will start comparing the counterfeits to my own work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, that's more like the reason Paimon had in mind.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Ever since that rumor started, three new perfumes claiming to be made from the Auguste flower have appeared on the market.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: If I can dispel the fanaticism surrounding "Auguste" — even just by proving the rumor to be false — Fontaine's perfume market can finally start to get back to normal.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Then, I'll be free from all the "stories" and "added meaning," and can focus on making what I like.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That makes sense...

choices.text: Either way, even if it's not for Mora...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Oh... I would, of course, be grateful for your help, but I wouldn't want to trouble you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, you said it yourself! We're both travelers from abroad, so "it's only right that we help each other out!"

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Hah... I suppose you're right. Then, you have my thanks.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Based on the information I have so far, it's unclear if the rumor is true.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Mr. Edgar also thinks it's too early to say... But you could always go talk to him? He was there all those years ago, after all... Maybe he'll know something.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Ah, I was just about to pay him a visit at the hotel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Edgar...? Who's that?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: The person you've been trying to guess this whole time — the "Flower Expert" in charge of the exhibition. He's also the most respected and experienced perfumer in the area.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Back when he was still working in Fontaine, "Auguste"... was his creation.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: I should also mention... He was my teacher, the one who taught me the basics of perfumery when I apprenticed in Sumeru.

choices.text: We could still help you out.
There's no way it's that easy to find...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I need to stay back and keep an eye on things here at the port. If something happens, don't hesitate to find me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, look at all the flowers!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Apparently, the exhibitor paid a large sum to rent out the hotel and surrounding buildings. They're being used as temporary storage facilities and lodging for exhibition personnel.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seems a bit excessive...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! What if guests come early? They won't have anywhere to stay! Also, renting out this big of a hotel... how are they gonna make that Mora back...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seems like they might have Mora to burn...
...It's been so long, I almost didn't recognize you, Edgar.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: ...Well, you and your brother haven't changed a bit.
All this catching up is nice and all, but let's get down to business! We need to talk about Kirya. Is he—

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Hold on... We have guests.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It's nice to see you again, Master.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Emilie... Is that you, haha? It's been years... Look at you! You're all grown up!

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: I've heard you've become quite the famous perfumer in Fontaine. It would seem the student has surpassed the master...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to your mentorship.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Ah! Hardly, hardly... I taught you the basics. Hearing you call me "Master," well, I'm not sure I'm deserving of that title.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: I've taught many students here in Sumeru over the years, but I've yet to see one turn out quite as accomplished as you... You're the only one who can take credit for that success!

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: And who are these two...? I don't recall you mentioning them in your letter...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: #Ah, they're my new friends, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pleasure to meet you, Mr. Edgar.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Emilie's friends? Well then, the pleasure is all mine.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: And these two gentlemen... Are they friends of yours, Master?
Hmph...
Uh... Haha, of course! We're perfume merchants from Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: I'm... Eude! And this, here, is my younger brother, Blaise. Edgar and the two of us are old friends... Isn't that right, gentlemen?

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: ...Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Merchant brothers...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You must be here to look for the Auguste flower, then!

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: ...Haha, well, what respectable perfume merchant hasn't heard of "Auguste"? Anyone in the business would be interested in the rumors.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: I'm guessing you're here for the same reason, Emilie? We were just about to get into it, so you three might as well join in.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: I commissioned a few Eremites to do some scouting for me. They searched all over Sumeru, but there were no sightings of the Auguste flower.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: That being said, there are people in Port Ormos who claim to have smelled a unique fragrance on the streets... definitely floral, but still distinct...

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Some of them were merchants who lived in Fontaine twenty years ago. According to them, the fragrance smelled exactly like the "Auguste" they remember from back then...

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: A "one of a kind," "divine," and "noble" scent...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe someone around here just happens to have a bottle of "Auguste" from back then?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: No, I don't think so. I doubt that's the case. Even if someone had a bottle that was never opened, the fragrance of the perfume would have changed over time. Very few perfumes can go decades without a change in scent...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: "Auguste" is even more prone to that kind of shift. Only a few bottles still exist in Fontaine, and their scent would have completely degraded by now.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Although... could there be a flower out there with a similar fragrance? Or an accord with the same base notes?

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: Impossible! If "Auguste" were that easy to replicate, it would never have sold for such a high price all those years ago! The Auguste flower is back! It has to be!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Technically speaking, the scent wouldn't be impossible to imitate...

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Well, let's table that question for now. Edgar, did any of those people mention where the scent was coming from?

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: ...No. By the time they realized they had smelled something, the scent was already gone. If I hadn't asked about it, they probably wouldn't have given the experience a second thought.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Compared to things we see and hear, smells can be much easier to overlook...

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Hmm... It almost sounds like someone wearing the "Auguste" fragrance passed them on the street...

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: Wait, are you saying...

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Ah, just thinking out loud, haha. Don't pay me any mind.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: We don't have much to go off of right now, but we can't rule out that possibility. I'll send some more people to investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: You all traveled so far to be here, why don't you rest in the hotel for a bit? Uh... Eude, Blaise, this is the key to your room.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, you've got the keys to the rooms? Do we get free lodging too?

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Ah... My apologies. All the rooms in the hotel are accounted for, I'm afraid. Most are being used for storage ahead of the exhibition, you see.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: I managed to tidy up one of the rooms for these two at the last minute... But, by the time Emilie wrote to me, there was no more space left for her to stay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and we just showed up out of the blue... Guess that means there's definitely no space for us.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I should've been more considerate. Here I am with an entire hotel at my disposal, and no place to offer you to stay... even after you made the trip all the way to Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Master. I can sleep on the boat tonight. Or, I could even camp in the wild. It would give me the opportunity to collect some plant specimens while I'm here in Sumeru.

choices.text: I'm familiar with the Sumeru wilderness...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Ah, even better!

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Although... Would it be possible for me to leave some of my luggage here? It would be rather cumbersome to take it camping. It shouldn't take up too much space...

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: Well... About that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It seems like Edgar and the others don't want anyone to stay near the hotel... But, they're also trying not to arouse suspicion... I'm not just imagining things, am I?)

response.speaker: Eude
response.text: Haha... Of course! No trouble at all! My brother and I will keep an eye on them for you... as long as you don't mind, Mademoiselle!

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: ...Alright, then. Eude, why don't you take Emilie inside and find a suitable place for her luggage.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: I'll prepare some refreshments and join you in a bit.

choices.text: I'll come with.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, the smell of flowers is so strong! Didn't Edgar say he tidied up around here? There's still so many flowers...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon took a peek through the window earlier, and his house was packed with flowers! Looks like this exhibition is gonna be huge!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do all perfumers have houses filled with flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...No. That's a Florist thing.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: We work closely with the essential oils of various plants, but to maintain a sharp sense of smell, most perfumers prefer to keep their homes free of strong odors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh... Guess there's just too much to store for the exhibition, then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's behind this door?

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Ah, this room seems to be a connected suite. My brother will be staying on the other side of the suite.

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Blaise... While you're out, why don't you bring our luggage over as well...

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Ahem... Blaise!

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: Ah... Yes, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Alright, then... Where can we find your luggage, Mademoiselle? Blaise will go fetch it for you.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It's still at the port. In addition to some daily necessities, there's also a case of Amber Wine that I brought back from Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Could I trouble you to bring that back as well? It would be the perfect way to repay you for your hospitality.

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Haha, how generous! I should thank you on my brother's behalf. You've stumbled upon his weakness! He's aloof about most things, but alcohol is his one true love.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Is that so?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Amber Wine... Now that's a Fontaine specialty I've never heard of before...)

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Mr. Eude, Mr. Blaise... Thanks for—

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: ...Hey! What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Argh!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: That's... Master's voice!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Quick! Let's go see what's going on!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you rush out of the hotel, you detect a unique fragrance coming from outside...

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: ...Edgar!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Master!

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: Hey, Edgar! Are you alright? Can you hear me?

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Who did this?

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: K—Kirya... "Auguste"...!

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: ...Kirya!

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: Hey! Edgar! Edgar!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: No, don't shake him. He's injured. Just leave him to me. You two can...

choices.text: We'll investigate the scene.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...Oh, thank you.

choices.text: We'll try to see where the culprit went.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That strange smell around here... Is it coming from this bottle?

dialogues.speaker: Bottles
dialogues.text: (Only a small amount of liquid is left inside the bottle, and streaks of residue can be seen on both the mouth and the sides of the vessel. It seems like someone forcibly poured out whatever was inside the bottle...)

choices.text: I have a feeling...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *gasp* Really? You think so?

choices.text: The liquid in this bottle is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think whoever did this was hiding in the flowers before they attacked Edgar?

dialogues.speaker: Check Flower Beds
dialogues.text: (There are no footprints in the flower beds... And it doesn't look like any of the branches or leaves have been disturbed...)

choices.text: Unless the culprit was your size...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm, true...

choices.text: That would be pretty difficult.

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: I checked... It doesn't look like anyone passed through here.

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: But that's impossible... It's not like that kid can just grow some wings and fly away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That kid?

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... the culprit, I mean! It's not like the culprit could have just disappeared into thin air!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Well, we looked all over, but the only clue we found was that bottle...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: The most important thing we can do now is focus our efforts on treating Master. Can you help me move him inside?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Absolutely.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... How's he doing?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: When I administered emergency treatment, I discovered a residue in his nose and mouth... Master was most likely forced to ingest a certain liquid.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: He's still unconscious, and inducing vomiting could obstruct his airways... We'll have to look into other clues for now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We found this bottle just now...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Ah, yes... The scent is the same, but the chemical composition is still unclear. We'll have to do further tests to determine if it's the same liquid. And how toxic it is to the human body.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: But, first... I do believe there are two people who could shed some light on the situation...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Mr. Sylvain, Mr. Lucien...

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: Wait, you—!

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Hey...!

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: ...Were you talking to us, Mademoiselle? I'm afraid we've never heard of those names before...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Hmm... Before arriving in Sumeru, I asked a friend from the Special Patrol to look into the creators of "Auguste"...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: There were four people in total... The perfumer, Edgar — the one thrust into the limelight — and three others...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: A researcher from Sumeru responsible for cultivating the Auguste flower... and two merchant brothers responsible for promoting the product on the market...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: The two brothers capitalized on the mythos surrounding "Auguste." Their actions lured in numerous speculators and profiteers, inflating the price of "Auguste" even further.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: In the end, they were sent to the Fortress of Meropide for falsifying their accounts and destabilizing the market... If you do the math, they should be out of prison by now.

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: Hmph! And what does that have to do with us? There are countless merchant families in Fontaine... You gonna accuse them of being criminals too?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Every time your brother called you "Blaise," it took you several seconds to respond... But, when I called you "Lucien" just now, the name registered immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: Ah, Miss Emilie... Out of respect for your position as a famous perfumer in Fontaine, I'm inclined to believe that was simply a poor attempt at humor.

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: You have a bright future ahead of you. You wouldn't want to develop a reputation as someone who throws around false accusations... especially among merchant circles.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Hmm... You claim to be regular perfume merchants, and yet... When I brought up "Amber Wine," you took it to be alcohol...

dialogues.speaker: Eude
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Just as I thought...)

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: "Amber Wine" is a perfume I created several years ago. It wasn't particularly renowned, but I'm certain any respectable perfume merchant in Fontaine would know of it.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Unless, until recently, they were living somewhere completely cut off from the perfume world... Hmm, somewhere like... the Fortress of Meropide perhaps...?

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: Emilie, you little...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't even think about it.

dialogues.speaker: Blaise
dialogues.text: Oof...!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Don't misunderstand, Mr. Sylvain. I don't bring this up to criticize you. No matter what happened all those years ago, the court has already passed its judgment.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: But Master's life is in danger. We need to learn whatever we can about the person who has done this.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: If Master's attack had something to do with "Auguste," I would imagine the two of you might also be in danger.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: So, I'd like to trouble you for some information, if I may... Tell me about "Kirya."

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: ...Fine. As you wish.

dialogues.speaker: Lucien
dialogues.text: ...Sylvain!

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: Lucien, if this will help us find Kirya, then it will be all worth it. Besides, we've already told most of this stuff to the Maison Ordalie, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: ...You were right, Miss Emilie, there were four of us at the beginning: Myself, Lucien, Edgar... and a researcher from Sumeru in charge of flower cultivation... Vijava.

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: Some time down the road, the Marechaussee Phantom came knocking, saddled us with a list of accusations, and started looking into our books... They did their meddling, and my brother, Edgar, and I were forced to serve time in the Fortress as a result...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like he's still upset about that... Wait, then how did Edgar end up in Sumeru?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Master was convicted as an accomplice, so he only had to serve a few years. He decided to move to Sumeru so that he could put those events behind him.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Still, Master was depressed for a long time after that... He stopped making new perfumes and focused on introducing students to the craft instead.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: That's how I met him. My parents had to relocate to Sumeru for work when I was a child, so I had the chance to study under him for a little while.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...But, we can talk about that some other time. I want to hear more about this researcher... Vijava.

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: ...Like us, Vijava was also staring down an investigation from the Marechaussee Phantom.

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: But, before the Phantom showed up at her door, she set all the flowerbeds on fire, along with much of the Mora we managed to earn. All the Auguste flowers, everything we worked to create... was reduced to nothing but a pile of ash.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... destroying all that evidence... Wouldn't that make things worse for her?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It didn't matter at that point... Because she died in the fire as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Lucien
dialogues.text: Hmph, sounds like you did an investigation of your own. Why even ask us if you knew all of this already?

choices.text: So far...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: The name wasn't mentioned in any of the files I reviewed, either. But... you two seem quite familiar with him.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: ...Kirya was Vijava's younger brother.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: He was just a clueless kid back then... somewhere in his teens, I think. He helped his sister with her work sometimes, but that was pretty much it... He didn't have any idea what we were doing.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Vijava kept him close most of the time. The three of us were probably the only ones who even knew she had a brother.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: After our operation was compromised, he disappeared... There were no signs of him until recently, when people started saying the Auguste flower had reappeared in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...So, you think Kirya took something with him back then... something that allowed him to reproduce the Auguste flower?

response.speaker: Lucien
response.text: Hmph, Vijava doted on the kid like you wouldn't believe! She even told us to give her cut to her brother if anything happened to her.

response.speaker: Lucien
response.text: If she left something behind before she died, believe me — Kirya's the one that has it!

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: And judging by the liquid in that bottle... the Auguste flower wasn't the only thing he reproduced... He managed to replicate the perfume itself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So the liquid Edgar was forced to ingest really was "Auguste"! Wait, does that mean "Auguste" is poison?

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Ahem! Poison? No, no... of course not! No perfume is meant to be ingested. Even small amounts can be dangerous, let alone ingesting a whole bottle at once.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: If "Auguste" could be considered a poison, we wouldn't have even sold half a bottle back then. Edgar fell unconscious because Kirya forced him to drink perfume... it just happened to be "Auguste"!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Strange... Sylvain seems nervous all of a sudden...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why did Kirya attack Edgar?

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Hah... He probably thought we had something to do with his sister's death. But, to tell you the truth, I have no idea why she did all that.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: We're not looking for Kirya because we have it out for him... We just wanted to see how he was doing... and, if possible, work together to bring back "Auguste."

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: We only went to prison for a bit of fraud and market manipulation... It had nothing to do with the product itself.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: As long as we keep things honest this time around... bringing the product back to market would almost be like honoring his sister's memory!

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...So, that's why you never mentioned Kirya during your interrogation?

response.speaker: Lucien
response.text: ...Yes, exactly! We were just looking out for the kid!

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Anyway, that's all we know... If you're looking for information on what's in "Auguste" or what to do if you ingest it... there are only two people to ask — Edgar... or Kirya himself.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...Well, at least we're able to say for certain that the substance Edgar ingested was, in fact, "Auguste." That gives us a direction for further testing... Well, then, I'd say that was a very enlightening discussion.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Ah, well, glad to hear it.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Lucien, let's head back to the room and rest for a bit. With everything that's happened... There are things that need reconsidering...

response.speaker: Lucien
response.text: Yes, of course.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...They're still hiding something.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Ah, you think so too? Hmm, that does seem to be the case... Pity we don't have more evidence.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: But, based on Sylvain's tone of voice just now, I suspect further questioning will only result in more made-up answers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The way you exposed them like that, just based on a hunch... That was genius!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you really just a perfumer who looks after people in your spare time?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! Earlier you said you were only sort of a doctor... and that your patients were "unusual"...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Oh, yes. That's because most of the "patients" I encounter... are already dead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, you're a... forensic doctor?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Close... I'm actually a "forensic cleaner." Once the forensic team and the Marechaussee Phantom are done collecting evidence from the scene, I'm in charge of clearing away the final traces my "patients" leave on the world.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: In fact, with just a small alteration to the formula, the same tincture used as the base of perfume can also be made into a cleaning agent.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Basically, there are two sides to forensics — those who collect evidence to expose the truth, and those who clean up the smells, bloodstains, and other substances left behind at the scene.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: I've learned a lot in my line of work, and I've witnessed a lot of death... But this time, we may still save the patient.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: #Actually, {NICKNAME}, could I trouble you to report back to Tighnari and the officers at Port Ormos? We should update them on the situation...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Will do.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: I'll stay here and continue to look after Master. Now that we have a sample of "Auguste"... I'm hoping further analysis won't be too difficult.

choices.text: Kirya's name still hasn't come up.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Woah, why the rush? Did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain everything...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: What!? Edgar was attacked?

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: He's the most famous perfumer in the region, someone who's helped countless people around Port Ormos... How could this happen...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Sheriff, have you received any reports of a suspicious individual fleeing through the bazaar?

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: No... But we've got eyes all over the area. I'm sure someone's seen Kirya.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: I'll start gathering my forces. We won't let him get away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about you, Tighnari? Do you have a plan?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'm sure the sheriff can handle things over at the scene, and I doubt Emilie needs my help looking after Mr. Edgar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... But, she said she's not a real doctor...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Then, she was far too modest. She may not be a doctor by trade, but she has a deeper understanding of human anatomy and pharmacology than most scholars from the Amurta Darshan.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Not to mention the fact that Mr. Edgar's condition is related to perfume... Emilie is certainly in the best position to help him.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As for me... I'll head to the Akademiya and see what I can learn about Vijava and Kirya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that's right! Vijava was supposed to be a scholar from Sumeru... Do you recognize the name?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: From Emilie's letter, certainly, but that was the first time I'd heard of it. The Akademiya produces a lot of scholars, and there are plenty of graduates who choose to pursue a career outside their Darshan.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I didn't have time to look into it earlier... But, now, it seems like Vijava's past could be critical to getting to the bottom of what happened to Mr. Edgar.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I have friends in Sumeru City that can help me investigate. With any luck, we'll have news to share by tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...I'll leave you and Emilie to watch over things here in Port Ormos.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: I'm sorry I couldn't offer you a room...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It's alright, Master. I know it was sudden.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: I'll be sure to make it up to you with a nice cup of tea.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Skin is flushed, pupils are dilated... But he's still breathing...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Master looks a lot older than when I last saw him... I just hope he can hold on...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Sylvain and his brother seem wary of us... We should leave them be for now. We don't want to spook them.)

dialogues.speaker: Perfume Bottles
dialogues.text: (There's only a small amount of liquid left in the bottle. According to Sylvain, the liquid is none other than the famed "Auguste" perfume.)

dialogues.speaker: Flower Stand
dialogues.text: (The stand displays flowers from various nations. Looking at the flower pot in the middle, the soil seems to have been disturbed recently.)

dialogues.speaker: Flowers
dialogues.text: (The neat rows of flowers were just so tempting, I really wanted to pick some... My hand just stretched out on its own... But when I thought of Tighnari's serious face, I managed to yank my hand back in time.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, this guy was a famous perfumer in Fontaine... But then, he came to Sumeru to... teach people from Fontaine? Sounds confusing...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It's a long story. If you're interested, we can talk more about it when we see him. He should be staying near the hotel.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Emilie carefully move Edgar inside...
